cf.title: pgcrypto: Fix sha-crypt rounds= values that do not fit in int (BUG #19743)

input.subject: [PATCH] pgcrypto: Fix sha-crypt rounds= values that do not fit in int (BUG #19743)

verdict_reasoning: No objection survived. The only one raised, standards-compat-1, was refuted: per message #9, strtoint() already saturates on REL_18_STABLE, so the patch changes only NOTICE text and tests there. The change is a fix for a reported bug (BUG #19743) inside existing pgcrypto code, reusing the existing clamp-with-NOTICE path. Confidence is medium because only 3 of 13 messages and the v1 patch prose were read.

brief.title: pgcrypto: clamp sha-crypt rounds= values that overflow int
brief.problem: crypt() parses the rounds= option of a sha256crypt or sha512crypt salt with strtoint() and never checks for overflow, so values beyond int wrap modulo 2^32 before clamping. rounds=4294968296 silently hashes with 1000 rounds and no NOTICE. This affects users who pass raw salt strings instead of using gen_salt() (BUG #19743).
brief.proposed_design: Out-of-range rounds= values now reach the existing clamp to PX_SHACRYPT_ROUNDS_MIN or PX_SHACRYPT_ROUNDS_MAX with a NOTICE. v2 used strtoi64(), and v4 went back to strtoint() after commit 426551c8cf49 made it saturate on overflow. The clamp NOTICEs echo the token as supplied, capped at 10 characters plus "...".
user_visible_surface: crypt() with $5$ or $6$ salts: overflowing rounds= values now clamp with a NOTICE instead of wrapping silently.
Clamp NOTICE text now shows the rounds token as supplied, truncated to 10 characters with "..." appended.
Non-canonical tokens such as rounds=+10 or rounds=010 now appear verbatim in the NOTICE.
author_claims: The fix is backpatchable to REL_18_STABLE, the only branch with sha-crypt support.
Negative rounds values keep the existing clamp behaviour; making them an ERROR belongs in a separate master-only change.
The pgcrypto regression suite passes 25/25 and core regression passes.
An unbounded 10000-digit token produced a NOTICE of about 10000 characters before the print cap.
brief.thread_state: Takeshi Ideriha shaped the design, and Chao Li reviewed v5 and said it looks good. Chao Li will propose a separate patch to reject an empty rounds= value. Negative-value errors are deferred to another discussion.
unclear: The patch prose for v2 to v5 is not shown, so the final commit message and test changes are unknown.
The positive-overflow tests depend on statement_timeout, and the material does not say whether they are stable on slow buildfarm animals.
The thread does not say whether a committer has agreed to backpatch, or whether the v4 strtoint() change depends on commit 426551c8cf49 being present on every target branch.

refuted.title: Backpatch changes hash output for salts that already wrap
refuted.failure_scenario: An application keeps a fixed raw salt such as '$6$rounds=4294968296$...' and checks passwords with crypt(pw, that_salt). After a REL_18 minor update, the same call clamps to 999999999 rounds instead of 1000. The result no longer matches stored hashes, and each call runs for a very long time, so logins fail or hang.
refuted.argument: The thread presents the change as safe to backpatch (messages #3, #4, #9), but for every overflowing token it changes which hash crypt() returns. Today such tokens give a deterministic, fast result, and some deployments may depend on it. Verification with crypt(pw, stored_hash) is likely unaffected, because the stored hash carries the effective rounds value. The thread does not separate that common case from callers that reuse the original raw salt, and it does not weigh the change against minor-release stability.
refuted.author_must_show: Does crypt() embed the effective rounds in its output, so that only callers reusing the raw overflowing salt change results, and is that acceptable in a minor release?

critic.reasoning: Message #9 says commit 426551c8cf49 already made strtoint() saturate and is on REL_18_STABLE, so overflowing tokens reach the existing clamp there without this patch. On that branch v5 changes only the NOTICE text and tests, so it does not cause the hash change described.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: An overflowing rounds= value no longer yields a silently weaker 1000-round password hash.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The author proposes a backpatch to REL_18_STABLE, and the NOTICE text changes for tokens such as rounds=+10.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Is commit 426551c8cf49 present on every branch targeted for backpatch, so that strtoint() saturates there as v4 and v5 assume?
Are the positive-overflow tests stable under statement_timeout on slow or heavily loaded buildfarm animals, or can they be written without a timeout?
Is the changed NOTICE text for in-range non-canonical tokens such as rounds=+10 and rounds=010 acceptable in a REL_18 minor release?
What does the final v5 commit message say about the behaviour change on master versus REL_18_STABLE?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows pgcrypto's crypt() code and the backpatch rules for contrib; neither reviewer is identified as a committer in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A small parsing and NOTICE change in contrib/pgcrypto/crypt-sha.c, plus regression tests that depend on statement_timeout and may need attention on slow buildfarm animals; a backpatch adds a NOTICE text change in a minor release.
committability.author_follow_up: The author answered review within a day and, per the brief, revised the patch through v5; this is a first submission, so there is no longer-term sign.

priority.reason: The fix affects only users who pass raw sha-crypt salts with overflowing rounds= values, but it closes a silent weakening of password hashes. The patch touches one source file and one test, and a reviewer has already said v5 looks good.

provisional_note: The v2 to v5 patch prose and the code were not read, so the final test design, the 10-character NOTICE cap and the dependence on commit 426551c8cf49 could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Upgrade pgcrypto to crypt_blowfish 1.3
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch ports upstream crypt_blowfish 1.3 into pgcrypto so that crypt() recognizes bcrypt hashes with the $2b$ prefix (and $2y$), keeping the Postgres-specific local changes. An earlier version only mapped $2b$ to the $2a$ code path, which Daniel Gustafsson rejected because the two variants handle the old bug differently.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the patch after it was added to the commitfest. After a cursory review and a fix for gcc warnings, it was returned in a batch of entries that lacked reviewer interest, with no objection to the patch itself.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more
community interest.

precedents_retrieved.title: Encoding protection for pgcrypto
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgp_sym_decrypt_text and pgp_pub_decrypt_text check that the decrypted result is valid in the database encoding, and raise an error if it is not. It adds regression tests for this and moves some existing tests that failed under some encodings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Cary Huang reported failing tests and questioned aborting the transaction instead of issuing a warning. The author posted v2 and argued that callers who want no encoding check can use the bytea variants, and no later message follows.

precedents_retrieved.title: Avoid obscure DES key buffer loop bounds in pgcrypto
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch replaces the `while (q - (uint8 *) keybuf - 8)` loop conditions in `px_crypt_des()` in pgcrypto's crypt-des.c with for-loops bounded by `sizeof(keybuf)`. The goal is clearer code and a workaround for a spurious gcc-16 -O3 -Wstringop-overflow warning caused by a gcc bug.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. A reviewer marked the patch Ready for Committer in August 2026, and no message raises an objection or explains the withdrawal.

precedents_retrieved.title: (DUPLICATE) Removing dead code in pgcrypto
precedents_retrieved.summary: Remove unused functions from pgcrypto in v16: mbuf_tell and mbuf_rewind, added in commit e94dd6ab91, and pgp_get_cipher_name. None of them is called in the tree, and pgp_get_cipher_name does not turn up in a search of extensions.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch drew no objections, and the reviewer said the change looked good. The entry was withdrawn as a duplicate commitfest entry: the author and the reviewer both registered the patch at about the same time.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I see a little race condition happen :) Sorry for this.

precedents_retrieved.title: Show subtransaction overflow status
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch exposes each backend's subtransaction count and whether its subtransaction cache has overflowed, so DBAs can find the sessions that force SLRU lookups for all concurrent queries. It started as two new pg_stat_activity columns and was reworked into a single function returning a record per backend.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that effort should go into fixing the subtransaction overflow performance problem itself, because monitoring does not relieve the problem and could cause compatibility problems once a fundamental fix changes how this area works. Andres Freund agreed and asked for the entry to be marked rejected, also noting it had been failing on cfbot for weeks. The author agreed that a real fix would make the status reporting pointless and marked it rejected.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support target_session_attrs=read-only and eliminate the added round-trip to detect session status.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a GUC that the server reports to clients through ParameterStatus, so clients learn without polling whether the session is on a hot standby and when the standby is promoted. Later versions report a session_read_only parameter and let libpq use it for target_session_attrs, including a new read-only value, without an extra round-trip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson returned the patch in October 2017 because questions raised in the thread were not answered. Open points in the visible messages include a failing recovery TAP test, inverted read-write/read-only checks in libpq, and the author's own concern that a read-only primary cannot be told apart from a standby. In November Michael Paquier closed it again because the patch no longer applied and there were no updates or replies.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Based on the unaddressed questions raised in this thread, I’m marking this
patch Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support target_session_attrs=read-only and eliminate the added round-trip to detect session status.
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Daniel Gustafsson, Michael Paquier, Andres Freund
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch has the server report the session's hot-standby or read-only state to clients through a ParameterStatus message, so clients learn it at connect time and when the server leaves hot standby. libpq would use this to support target_session_attrs=read-only without an extra round-trip to check the session state.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Questions raised in review went unanswered, and later versions stopped applying to master. Thomas Munro reported that the recovery test 001_stream_rep.pl failed with the patch. Melanie Plageman found that target_session_attrs=read-write rejected a primary server. The entry was moved to later commitfests without a new version, so Michael Paquier and Andres Freund marked it returned with feedback for lack of progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given that
there's been no progress for multiple commitfests, and this is the last
CF, this doesn't seem appropriate.

precedents_retrieved.title: Nonreplayable XLog records by means of overflows and >MaxAllocSize lengths
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds checks in xloginsert.c so that the WAL insertion API cannot assemble a record larger than xlogreader can read (MaxAllocSize, later a fixed 1020 MiB limit), and cannot overflow xl_tot_len through repeated XLogRegisterData() calls. It also documents the record size limit in the XLogRecord spec.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier committed part of the patch, the API changes and the uint16 block data checks. He then asked for a rebase of the rest, and the author did not reply for two commitfests, so the entry was returned with feedback. After it was closed, Andres Freund noted that the new record-too-large ERROR usually happens inside a critical section and so becomes a PANIC. He suggested building large records such as the commit record before the critical section.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
No replies after 4 weeks, so I have marked this entry as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Apply a better fix to mdunlinkfork().
Reverted commit(s): Use TRUNCATE to preserve relfilenode for pg_largeobject + index.; Fix failure to remove non-first segments of temporary tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Replace the stopgap fix I made in 0e758ae89 with a cleaner one.

The real problem with 4ab5dae94 is that it contorted this function's
logic substantially, by introducing a third code path that required
different behavior in the function's main loop.  That seems quite
unnecessary on closer inspection: the new IsBinaryUpgrade case can
just share the behavior of the other immediate-unlink cases.  Hence,
revert 4ab5dae94 and most of 0e758ae89 (keeping the latter's
save/restore errno fix), and add IsBinaryUpgrade to the set of
conditions tested to choose immediate unlink.

Also fix some additional places with sloppy handling of errno,
to ensure we have an invariant that we always continue processing
after any non-ENOENT failure of do_truncate.  I doubt that that's
fixing any bug of field importance, so I don't feel it necessary to
back-patch; but we might as well get it right while we're here.

Also improve the comments, which had drifted a bit from what the
code actually does, and neglected to mention some important
considerations.

Back-patch to v15, not because this is fixing any bug but because
it doesn't seem like a good idea for v15's mdunlinkfork logic to be
significantly different from both v14 and v16.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert refactoring of hex code to src/common/
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert refactoring of hex code to src/common/
Reverted commit(s): move hex_decode() to /common so it can be called from frontend; Rework refactoring of hex and encoding routines; Remove PG_SHA*_DIGEST_STRING_LENGTH from sha2.h
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This is a combined revert of the following commits:
- c3826f8, a refactoring piece that moved the hex decoding code to
src/common/.  This code was cleaned up by aef8948, as it originally
included no overflow checks in the same way as the base64 routines in
src/common/ used by SCRAM, making it unsafe for its purpose.
- aef8948, a more advanced refactoring of the hex encoding/decoding code
to src/common/ that added sanity checks on the result buffer for hex
decoding and encoding.  As reported by Hans Buschmann, those overflow
checks are expensive, and it is possible to see a performance drop in
the decoding/encoding of bytea or LOs the longer they are.  Simple SQLs
working on large bytea values show a clear difference in perf profile.
- ccf4e27, a cleanup made possible by aef8948.

The reverts of all those commits bring back the performance of hex
decoding and encoding back to what it was in ~13.  Fow now and
post-beta3, this is the simplest option.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P12] and [P17] cover integer parsing in front-end utilities and command-line options, not pgcrypto salt parsing, and neither records a reason. The thread points to no earlier discussion of this idea, only to the strtoint() change in message #9, which this patch builds on.
The other user-visible changes look acceptable from this angle. The NOTICE text now echoes the token, capped at 10 characters, and that changes no SQL syntax, GUC, catalog or dump behaviour.

The patch changes how crypt() parses one salt option and what one NOTICE prints. It adds no WAL records, catalog changes, on-disk format changes, protocol messages or extension API changes. Stored hashes keep working because verification reads the rounds value written into the stored hash, which this patch leaves unchanged.

From the security angle the change narrows a weakness: an overflowing rounds= value no longer gives a silently weaker 1000-round hash. A user could already ask for 999999999 rounds with an in-range value, so the clamp to the maximum adds no new denial-of-service path. The NOTICE echoes only the caller's own input, and message #6 and message #11 capped its length. Stored hashes keep the canonical rounds value, so verifying existing hashes is unaffected.

This is a small bug fix inside existing pgcrypto code, and it adds no GUC, catalog, API, dependency or hot-path cost. It uses strtoint() saturation that is already backpatched, and the overflow tests would catch a later change to that behaviour. The statement_timeout test stability and the backpatch decision are implementation or committer questions, outside this angle. Neither precedent's recorded reason applies.

This is a bug fix for silent wraparound in crypt() rounds= parsing, so no existing feature, extension or idiom gives users correct clamping for raw salt strings. gen_salt() avoids the bug but does not fix crypt() on caller-supplied salts. The patch reuses the existing clamp-with-NOTICE path and the existing strtoint() helper, so it adds no second mechanism.

This is a bug fix for a reported bug (BUG #19743), where crypt() silently hashes with 1000 rounds instead of the value given, with no NOTICE. A field report, a reproduction on master and agreement from two reviewers (messages #2, #13) are enough demand for a correctness fix. The cost stays inside pgcrypto's sha-crypt path, so the demand angle has no objection to send.
